newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate soars on soft peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate soars on soft peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up a sharp 170 basis points to 20.70 percent in later morning trade on Friday on what traders said was weakness on the peso.
"The peso is soft and those with liquidity in pesos are after higher rates of return in secondary money market," a fixed-income analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour pesos had pared an earlier slide, but were still 1.4 centavos weaker at 7.9580/7.9600 per dollar in late morning dealing.
Another analyst agreed players with heavy peso positions were swaying the market.
"Investors are trying to take advantage of the weak peso and jack up interest rates," he said.
Dealers said secondary rates were also under pressure from corporate demand for cash to pay tax bills.
Overnight rates on bank paper also succumbed to upside pressure and had increased by 170 basis points to 21.40 percent.
Liquidity of 10.188 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
